content.value_statement: Agents lose useful context when memory is not designed carefully. This skill helps teams choose and implement vector, graph, and temporal memory layers.
actual_capabilities: Explains memory layers from working context to persistent storage.
Compares vector stores, knowledge graphs, and temporal knowledge graphs.
Provides Python examples for vector search and graph-based memory.
Shows temporal validity patterns for time-aware fact retrieval.
Describes memory consolidation and context injection patterns.
limitations: The Python code is educational and not production hardened.
Embedding generation is simulated and must be replaced in real systems.
It does not provide a complete database or hosted memory service.
Privacy, retention, and access controls require separate implementation.

use_cases.title: Design persistent support memory
use_cases.description: Plan memory layers that remember customer entities, preferences, and past issues across support sessions.

use_cases.title: Prototype graph-based agent memory
use_cases.description: Use the sample structures to model entities, relationships, and temporal facts before choosing infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Evaluate memory architecture tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare vector retrieval, graph traversal, and temporal queries for accuracy, latency, and complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a memory layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the memory-systems skill to recommend a memory layer for my agent. The agent must remember user preferences across sessions. Explain the tradeoffs in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Plan entity memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for consistent entity tracking.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the memory-systems skill to design entity memory for a workflow assistant. Include entity types, relationships, retrieval patterns, and consolidation needs.

prompt_templates.title: Prototype temporal facts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation planning for time-aware memory.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the memory-systems skill to outline a temporal knowledge graph for changing customer account facts. Include valid-from, valid-until, query, and conflict handling patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a memory architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the memory-systems skill to review this agent memory design. Identify missing layers, retrieval risks, scaling limits, privacy concerns, and concrete implementation changes.

output_examples.input: Design memory for an assistant that remembers project decisions across sessions.
output: Use short-term session memory for active tasks and long-term graph memory for decisions.
Store each decision with entities, source, timestamp, and confidence.
Retrieve by project entity first, then use semantic search for related notes.

output_examples.input: Compare vector RAG and temporal knowledge graphs for user profile history.
output: Vector RAG is simpler and works well for broad semantic lookup.
Temporal knowledge graphs are better when facts change and old values must remain queryable.
Use temporal validity when the assistant must answer what was true at a past date.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed memory consolidation process.
output: Consolidate when duplicate facts grow or outdated facts appear in retrieval.
Merge by entity and relationship type, then preserve source and confidence metadata.
Rebuild indexes after consolidation and test retrieval quality.

best_practices: Match the memory architecture to the queries the agent must answer.
Store source, timestamp, confidence, and validity metadata with durable facts.
Consolidate memories on a schedule and after major knowledge changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use a vector store when relationship traversal is the core requirement.
Do not treat outdated facts as current without temporal validity checks.
Do not inject large memory dumps into context without ranking and limits.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design agent memory systems that persist state, track entities, and retrieve useful facts across sessions.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes educational Python examples for vector stores, property graphs, temporal graphs, and integration patterns.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: No. The examples show architecture patterns and need real embeddings, storage, validation, and security controls.

faq.question: When should I use temporal memory?
faq.answer: Use temporal memory when facts change over time and the agent must know which fact was valid at a date.

faq.question: Can this work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documentation-based and can guide architecture work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace a graph database?
faq.answer: No. It explains graph memory patterns, but production systems still need a suitable database or storage layer.
